battle.name: 阿倍比羅夫
battle.brief: 658年（齊明天皇四年），越國國司阿倍比羅夫率水軍一百八十艘，向東北與北海道一線的蝦夷諸部及肅慎出兵。蝦夷首領恩荷率津輕、山本兩郡蝦夷歸降，渡島蝦夷集結大饗而還，朝廷另得生熊二頭、熊皮七十張。卡面的秦連弩是漢代弩機技術，飛鳥時代倭軍用的是大和弓與短刀太刀，此役並無連弩在場。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭發生在七世紀中葉的東北亞，是倭國飛鳥時代朝廷對北方與東北地區諸部族的一連串軍事行動，並非兩個國家之間的戰爭。倭方由齊明天皇（天豐財重日足姬天皇）下詔出兵，阿倍比羅夫以越國國司之身總領水軍，兵員以大和的弓師、刀士與水手為主，輔以受降後編入的部族成員。對面是東北地方到北海道一線的蝦夷諸部，包含津輕郡、山本郡（渟代）、渡島、飽田、膽振等部族，以及被史書單獨列出的肅慎部；這些部族沒有常備的國家軍隊，靠首領率眾、村落據點與對天候的熟悉作戰。值得注意的是渡島的蝦夷人站在倭方一邊，在遠征中充當嚮導與協力者；受降之後，部分部眾被編入朝廷的郡縣體系，由新設的郡領管轄。整體而言，這是一場以飛鳥朝廷為主動方、以北方部族聯盟為對手的邊疆經略，其成果在三年之後被延伸運用到半島戰線，663年的白江口之戰則是另一場戰爭。
countriesEn: This war was fought in the mid seventh century in northeast Asia, and it was a series of military operations by the court of Yamato in the Asuka period against tribal groups in the north and the northeast, not a war between two states. The Japanese side acted on the order of Empress Jimei, the emperor Temmu Toyo-kanchi-Hime no Mikoto, and Abe no Hirafu, provincial governor of Kosi, took command of the water force; the troops were the bowmen, the swordsmen and the boat crews of Yamato, with contingents of tribal people drawn in after their submission. Opposite them were the Emishi peoples from Tohoku as far as Hokkaido, including the groups of Tsugaru district, of Yamato (Unatai) district, of Watashi, of Hoda and of Sappu, together with the Sushen, whom the chronicles list as a people apart. These groups had no standing national army and fought through their chiefs, through their village strongholds and through their familiarity with the weather. It is worth noting that the Emishi of Watashi stood on the Japanese side and acted as guides and auxiliaries in the expedition; and after their submission some of the tribal people were drawn into the governmental system of the court as districts under newly appointed district governors. In sum this was a frontier campaign in which the Asuka court took the offensive against a loose tribal coalition in the north, whose results were later applied to the peninsula front, while the Battle of Baekgang of 663 was a separate war.
people: 這場戰爭的主角是阿倍比羅夫，姓阿倍，名比羅夫，《日本書紀》稱他為阿倍引田臣，《大日本史》作阿部比羅夫。他是越國出身的豪族，齊明天皇時任越國國司，領兵於東北，並在水軍行動中擔任統帥。據《日本書紀》，658年他率水軍一百八十艘討伐蝦夷，蝦夷首領恩荷率津輕、山本（渟代）兩郡的蝦夷歸降，他召集渡島的蝦夷大饗而歸；同年又討伐肅慎，獲得生熊二頭、熊皮七十張，歸獻天皇。659年他再討蝦夷，兼併飽田、渟代、津輕、膽振諸部，於後方羊蹄一帶設置郡領，擊敗肅慎並俘虜四十九人。660年他再以二百艘戰船出征，在大河一帶遇上肅慎軍隊，藉渡島人的協助於奧尻島擊敗對手，並獻俘於天皇。662年百濟求援，天智天皇任命他為後將軍兼征新羅將軍，率倭軍進入半島，663年在白江口大敗而還，事後被任為大宰帥鎮守九州北部。他另有子阿倍宿奈麻呂，同樣是北渡的武官，其家系日後更出使唐廷的阿倍仲麻呂，成為倭唐交通的代表人物。
peopleEn: The central figure of this war was Abe no Hirafu, of the surname Abe and the personal name Hirafu, called Abe no Hirafu-den no Otomo in the Nihon Shoki and Abe no Hirafu in the Dainihonshi. He was a member of a powerful clan of the province of Kosi, and in the reign of Empress Jimei he held the office of provincial governor of Kosi, leading troops in the northeast and taking command of the naval operations. According to the Nihon Shoki, in 658 he took a water force of one hundred and eighty ships against the Emishi; the Emishi chief Engaku led the Emishi of Tsugaru and of Yamato (Unatai) to surrender, and Abe gathered the Emishi of Watashi for a great banquet and returned. In the same year he also campaigned against the Sushen, taking two living bears and seventy sheets of bear hide, which he presented to the emperor. In 659 he campaigned against the Emishi again, taking in the groups of Hoda, Unatai, Tsugaru and Sappu, and set up a district governor in the region of Kitatobe (the area of the present Hidaka in Hokkaido); he defeated the Sushen again and took forty-nine prisoners. In 660 he sailed once more with two hundred warships, met a Sushen force on the great river, and with the help of the people of Watashi defeated them on the island of Okushiri, presenting the captives to the emperor. In 662 Paekche appealed for aid, and Emperor Tenji appointed him rear general and commander for the expedition against Silla, taking the Japanese army into the Korean peninsula; in 663 his army was badly beaten at Baekgang, after which he was made governor of the Tsushima office to hold the northern part of Kyushu against Silla and Tang. He had a son, Abe no Sukemaro, who was likewise a commander on northern expeditions; from the same line came later Abe no Nakamaro, the envoy to the Tang court and a byword for Japanese-Chinese contact.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩屬於漢代的弩機技術：弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。技術起於戰國，成熟於兩漢，但到七世紀中葉，連弩的連發機構早已不是東亞軍隊的制式裝備，實際上不可能出現在這場戰爭的現場；日本飛鳥時代的軍隊使用的是弓、刀、盾與甲冑，並沒有可靠記載顯示倭國在這次北渡中攜帶漢式連弩，北方部族用的則是更簡單的弓矢與近身兵器。倭方軍械的骨架是非對稱形制的大和弓，這種長弓射速快、適合在北方開闊海岸與林間射擊，配以短刀與太刀作為主要近戰兵器；士卒常備木製或竹製的盾，重要的軍人穿具足一類的甲冑，並攜帶長柄的槍與矛。船隊是這次行動最關鍵的裝備，一百八十艘與二百艘的數目都是《日本書紀》所記的水軍船隻，屬於能在東北海岸外海與內海之間迅速轉移的近海舟型。北方部族方面，蝦夷與肅慎以弓矢、木盾和皮甲作戰，善用結冰的灣汊與山嶺地形。生熊與熊皮不是武器，卻是這場戰爭中被明確記錄下來的戰利品與朝貢品。
kitsEn: The repeating crossbow on the card belongs to the Han technique of the crossbow lock: the lock stores the pull, and one tread sends one bolt. The idea originated in the Warring States and matured under the Han, but by the middle of the seventh century the repeating mechanism had long ceased to be standard equipment anywhere in East Asia, and it could not really have been present in this war; the army of the Asuka period in Japan used bows, swords, shields and armour, and no reliable record shows the Japanese taking a Chinese-style repeating crossbow on these northern expeditions, while the northern tribes used plainer bows and close-quarter weapons. The backbone of the Japanese armament was the asymmetrical yamato bow, a long bow with a fast draw that suited shooting along open northern coasts and in woodland, paired with the short sword and the great sword as the main close-combat arms; the men carried wooden or bamboo shields, the most important men wore armour of the suozoku type, and they also bore long-shafted spears and pikes. The ships were the most critical equipment of the operation, and the figures of one hundred and eighty and of two hundred are the water-force ships recorded in the Nihon Shoki, coastal craft of the type able to shift quickly between the outer sea and the inner waters of the northeastern coast. On the tribal side, the Emishi and the Sushen fought with bows and arrows, wooden shields and leather armour, and they used the frozen inlets and the mountain country well. The living bears and the bear hides were not weapons, but they are the booty and tribute items explicitly recorded for this war.
tactics: 倭方的戰法是「海路機動、登陸掃蕩、羈縻收編」三段式。先以集中的船隊沿海峽北進，在津輕、渟代與渡島一帶登陸，弓手列陣射擊壓制村落據點，步卒持短刀與槍逼近；擊破之後不以屠滅為終點，而是立即舉行大饗，把受降的部族首領與部眾收為朝廷的寄從部與郡民，讓其供給糧食、導引道路並參與後續出兵。對仍拒絕歸附的肅慎部，倭方改成遠距離追擊：先以船隊沿海岸搜索，再深入內陸的河川地帶，憑藉當地嚮導熟悉潮汐、風向與道路，最終在奧尻島一帶完成決戰。北方部族的戰術完全相反：避免集結與正面決戰，退入山間與內陸，利用村落、樹林和冬季結冰的灣汊拖住來犯者，在自己熟悉的地形裡以弓矢遲滯敵軍。北渡行動最實際的難題是季節與海況，東北外海冬季風浪大、灣口易結冰，船隊的補給與回程時程因此被牢牢限制在一年之中能通航的窗口內。
tacticsEn: The Japanese method ran in three stages: movement by sea, sweeping landings, and the tying of the defeated into the court system. A concentrated fleet first moved north along the coast, putting in to land around Tsugaru, Unatai and Watashi, where the archers were formed up to shoot and pin the village strongholds while spearmen and short-sword men closed in. The purpose was not to destroy the settlements but, once they were broken, to hold a great banquet at once, taking the surrendered chiefs and their people into the court as dependent settlers and district folk, so that they would supply food, show the roads and serve in later expeditions. Against the Sushen, who would not submit, the Japanese changed to a long pursuit: the fleet searched along the coast, then pushed inland up the river valleys, taking advantage of local guides who knew the tides, the winds and the tracks, and the decision was finally fought out in the neighbourhood of the island of Okushiri. The tactics of the northern tribes were the exact opposite: they avoided massing and avoided a set-piece engagement, falling back into the hills and the interior, and used their villages, their woods and the bays frozen over in winter to hold up the invaders, delaying the Japanese with arrows from country they knew. The most practical difficulty of the northern expeditions was the season and the state of the sea; the outer waters off the northeast are rough in winter and the mouths of the bays freeze over, and the supply of the fleet and the timing of the return were therefore bound closely to the window in which navigation was possible.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但幾個關鍵點相當明確：658年的水軍為一百八十艘；同年討伐肅慎所得為生熊二頭與熊皮七十張；659年設郡領於後方羊蹄一帶，俘虜肅慎四十九人；660年再出的戰船為二百艘。行程方面，遠征自畿內出發，經津輕、渟代海岸而至渡島，660年更北進至奧尻島一帶，奧尻位於北海道西岸、與本州隔海相望；三年之間連續北渡，說明這不是一次性的襲擊，而是有節奏的季節性行動。戰果方面，《日本書紀》只記錄倭方所得——歸降部眾、俘虜與熊皮，既沒有記載敵方的傷亡數字，也沒有記載己方的損失，這是飛鳥時代編年史常見的取捨：勝仗記功，敗績從略，因此本役的戰損數字無法從現存記載中推得，只能說不可考。時間上，658年至660年的三次出兵間隔約一年，正對應北方可以通航的季節窗口。
dataEn: There are not many figures that can be checked, but several key points are reasonably firm: the water force of 658 numbered one hundred and eighty ships; in the same year the campaign against the Sushen yielded two living bears and seventy sheets of bear hide; in 659 a district governor was set up in the region of Kitatobe, and forty-nine Sushen were taken prisoner; the warships sent out in 660 numbered two hundred. As for distance, the expedition set out from the capital region, worked along the Tsugaru and Unatai coasts to Watashi, and in 660 pushed further north to the neighbourhood of the island of Okushiri, which lies off the western coast of Hokkaido across the sea from Honshu; three expeditions in three consecutive years show that this was not a single raid but a season-by-season campaign. As for results, the Nihon Shoki records only what the Japanese side won, the surrendered communities, the captives and the hides, and records neither the enemy's losses nor the Japanese losses; this is the usual choice made by Asuka annalists, who note successes and pass over defeats, so the casualty figures for this war cannot be derived from the surviving record and can only be called unknown. In time, the three expeditions of 658, 659 and 660 were spaced about a year apart, matching the navigable season in the north.
cause: 直接起因是東北與北海道方向的諸部族陸續歸附、而另一些部族拒絕朝貢，朝廷需要把這條邊界固定下來。658年蝦夷首領恩荷率津輕、山本兩郡的蝦夷來降，飛鳥朝廷視之為機遇，隨即在同一年出兵肅慎，把勢力推向更北的北海道一線；次年再討蝦夷、兼併飽田、渟代、津輕、膽振諸部，並在後方羊蹄設置郡領，等於用律令體系的郡縣編制去承接剛取得的土地與人口。深一層看，這是飛鳥時代國家成形過程中的一環：大和朝廷正把早期的氏族聯盟與寄從部制度推向北方，把邊地部族納入朝貢羈縻、設置郡領，藉此把控制從飛鳥京畿一路延伸到津輕與日高。外部形勢同樣推著這場戰爭走：同一時期倭國在朝鮮半島與高句麗、百濟交戰，北方航線與沿海部族的穩定，正是這段時期可以倚靠的後方。
causeEn: The immediate cause was that tribal groups in the northeast and in Hokkaido were beginning to submit in their own way while others refused to pay tribute, and the court needed to fix this frontier in place. When the Emishi chief Engaku led the Emishi of Tsugaru and of Yamato to surrender in 658, the Asuka court took the opening, and in the same year campaigned against the Sushen, pushing its reach further north towards the Hokkaido line; the following year it campaigned against the Emishi again, absorbing the groups of Hoda, Unatai, Tsugaru and Sappu, and set up a district governor at Kitatobe, which amounted to using the district system of the ritsuryō order to take in land and people just acquired. At a deeper level this was one part of the making of the state in the Asuka period: the Yamato court was carrying the older clan alliances and the dependent-settlement system into the north, drawing frontier tribes into tribute and control and appointing district governors, and so extending its reach from the Asuka capital region right through to Tsugaru and the Hidaka coast. The wider situation pushed in the same direction; in these same years Japan was at war in the Korean peninsula against Goguryeo and Paekche, and a secure northern sea route and settled coastal tribes were exactly the reliable rear that the court could rely on.
impact: 這場戰爭最大的效果不在戰場，而在編制。恩荷所率部眾的歸附、渡島蝦夷的加入，以及659年後方羊蹄郡領的設置，使北方部族第一次被明確地納入朝廷的行政與貢納體系：受降者由獨立的部族變成有郡領、有戶口的編戶。這條政策在北方留下了延續數百年的制度痕跡，日本北海道最早的行政痕跡之一正來自這次設郡的記載。另一層後果是北方部族與大和朝廷之間形成了穩定的朝貢管道：生熊、熊皮一類的物產由戰場被帶回，俘虜被帶回京畿，倭方的鐵器、刀與馬具也沿著同一條航線流過去。此後阿倍氏成為以北事為專職的武官家族，北渡的經驗被一代代傳下去；到662年百濟求援、663年白江口一戰，倭國把兵力抽往半島，才發現北方經營所得的人力與船隻，遠不足以支撐另一場大規模的消耗戰。
impactEn: The largest effect of this war lay not on the battlefield but in the administrative system. The submission of the people led by Engaku, the joining of the Emishi of Watashi, and the establishment of a district governor at Kitatobe in 659 drew the northern tribes for the first time explicitly into the administrative and tributary order of the court: the surrendered went from being independent communities to being enrolled households under a named district governor. This policy left a trace in the north that would run for several hundred years, and one of the earliest signs of administration in Hokkaido comes precisely from the record of this establishment of a district. A second consequence was the formation of a steady line of tribute between the northern tribes and the Yamato court: living bears and bear hides were carried back from the field, captives were brought back to the capital region, and iron tools, swords and horse gear of the Japanese travelled the same route in the opposite direction. The Abe family thereafter became a line of commanders specialised in northern service, and the experience of the northern voyages was handed down generation by generation; when Paekche appealed in 662 and the army fought at Baekgang in 663, and Japan moved its strength to the peninsula, it became clear that the manpower and the shipping won in the north were far from enough to sustain another war of attrition on that scale.
result: 就658年這一場而言，結果是明確而直接的：蝦夷首領恩荷率津輕與山本（渟代）兩郡的蝦夷歸降，渡島的蝦夷被召集大饗後一同歸順，朝廷在同一年的另一路行動中討伐肅慎，獲得生熊二頭、熊皮七十張歸獻天皇。659年的續戰兼併了飽田、渟代、津輕、膽振諸部的蝦夷，肅慎再度被擊敗並被俘四十九人，且在後方羊蹄設立了郡領，把新取得的土地正式置於律令體制之下。660年第三次出兵以二百艘戰船在北方大河遇上肅慎軍隊，得渡島人協助，於奧尻島取勝並獻俘於天皇。整體而言，658年至660年三度北渡，蝦夷與肅慎各部不是被消滅，而是被分割、受降、編戶與設郡，北方航線與羈縻關係因此初步成形；但《日本書紀》對敵方損失幾無記載，這種沒有損失的印象來自編年史的取捨而非戰場實況，東北與北海道的抵抗並未因此告終。
resultEn: For 658 itself the outcome was direct and clear: the Emishi chief Engaku led the Emishi of Tsugaru and of Yamato (Unatai) to surrender, the Emishi of Watashi were gathered for a great banquet and came over with them, and in the other column of the same year the Sushen were campaigned against, yielding two living bears and seventy sheets of bear hide for presentation to the emperor. The campaign of 659 went on to absorb the Emishi of Hoda, Unatai, Tsugaru and Sappu, defeated the Sushen once more and took forty-nine of them prisoner, and set up a district governor at Kitatobe, placing the newly won land formally under the ritsuryō system. The third expedition, of 660, met a Sushen force with two hundred warships on the great river in the north, and with the help of the people of Watashi won at the island of Okushiri and presented captives to the emperor. Taken as a whole, the three northern expeditions of 658 to 660 did not destroy the Emishi and the Sushen; they divided them, took them by surrender, enrolled them as households and set districts over them, and a northern sea route and a network of tribute relations began to take shape. The Nihon Shoki, however, records almost nothing of the enemy's losses, so the impression of a war without cost comes from the choices of the annalist rather than from the state of the field, and resistance in the northeast and in Hokkaido was by no means ended by it.
